content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving opium tincture and various other medications. 1. Opium tincture and alvimopan: Alvimopan is contraindicated in opioid-tolerant patients, defined as those who have taken therapeutic doses of opioids for more than seven consecutive days prior to alvimopan administration. Recent opioid exposure increases sensitivity to alvimopan, potentially causing abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. 2. Olanzapine/samidorphan and opium tincture: Samidorphan, an opioid antagonist, reduces the effects of opium tincture through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of precipitating acute opioid withdrawal in opioid-dependent patients. A minimum opioid-free interval of 7 days for short-acting opioids and 14 days for long-acting opioids is recommended before initiating olanzapine/samidorphan. 3. Buprenorphine and opium tincture: The antagonist activity of buprenorphine may provoke withdrawal symptoms in opioid-dependent patients. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Opium tincture and calcium/magnesium/potassium/sodium oxybates: Co-administration may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use only when other treatment options are inadequate, limit dosages and durations, and monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation. 5. Cimetidine and opium tincture: Cimetidine increases the effects of opium tincture by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Clonidine and opium tincture: Co-administration enhances central nervous system (CNS) depressant effects, increasing toxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Desvenlafaxine and opium tincture: Both drugs increase serotonin levels, raising the risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Opium tincture and eluxadoline: Co-administration increases the risk of constipation-related serious adverse reactions. Avoid combining with other drugs that cause constipation. 9. Fentanyl and opium tincture: Co-administration with CNS depressants, such as skeletal muscle relaxants, may cause respiratory depression, hypotension, profound sedation, coma, or death. Consider dose reduction and monitor for adverse effects. 10. Isocarboxazid and opium tincture: This combination increases toxicity through an unknown mechanism, with risks of hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Avoid use and separate by 14 days. 11. Linezolid and opium tincture: Similar to isocarboxazid, this combination increases toxicity with risks of hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Avoid use and separate by 14 days. 12. Metoclopramide intranasal and opium tincture: Avoid use of metoclopramide intranasal or interacting drugs depending on the importance of the drug to the patient. 13. Nalbuphine and opium tincture: The antagonist activity of nalbuphine may provoke withdrawal symptoms in opioid-dependent patients. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Opium tincture and olopatadine intranasal: Co-administration increases the risk of CNS depression, leading to additive psychomotor impairment and daytime impairment. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Pentazocine and opium tincture: The antagonist activity of pentazocine may provoke withdrawal symptoms in opioid-dependent patients. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Phenelzine and opium tincture: This combination increases toxicity through an unknown mechanism, with risks of hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Avoid use and separate by 14 days. 17. Procarbazine and opium tincture: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) may potentiate CNS depression and hypotension. Avoid use within 14 days of MAOI administration. 18. Ropinirole and opium tincture: Narcotics, hypnotics, or sedatives can produce additive neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid use and monitor for excessive CNS toxicity. 19. Selegiline and opium tincture: This combination increases toxicity through an unknown mechanism, with risks of hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Sodium oxybate and opium tincture: Co-administration may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Reserve use for patients with inadequate alternative treatment options, limit dosages and durations, and monitor closely. 21. Tramadol and opium tincture: Tramadol may reinitiate opiate dependence in patients previously addicted to other opiates and provoke withdrawal symptoms in currently opioid-dependent patients. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Venlafaxine and opium tincture: Both drugs increase serotonin levels, raising the risk of serotonin syndrome. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Zuranolone and opium tincture: Co-administration with other CNS depressants may increase psychomotor impairment or CNS depressant effects. If unavoidable, consider dose reduction. 24. Opium tincture and sedative drugs (e.g., alprazolam, amitriptyline, baclofen, etc.): Co-administration increases sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Opium tincture and stimulants (e.g., amphetamine, caffeine, etc.): The interaction effect is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Opium tincture and MAOIs (e.g., tranylcypromine, phenelzine, etc.): Co-administration increases toxicity with risks of hypotension, hyperpyrexia, somnolence, or death. Avoid use and separate by 14 days. 27. Opium tincture and CNS depressants (e.g., benzodiazepines, barbiturates, etc.): Co-administration increases the risk of respiratory depression, hypotension, profound sedation, coma, or death. Use caution, consider dose reduction, and monitor closely.
